title: Ways to Split Graph Into K Components
statement:
You are given a **complete graph** on `N` labelled vertices `1..N`: every pair of distinct vertices is joined by exactly one edge, so there are `N * (N - 1) / 2` edges.

You may delete any subset of the edges (including none of them or all of them). Two choices are different if the sets of deleted edges are different.

Count the choices after which the remaining graph has **exactly `K` connected components** (an isolated vertex is a component). Because the count can be huge, print it modulo `M`. Note that `M` is not necessarily prime.
input_format: A single line containing three integers `N`, `K` and `M`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the number of valid edge-deletion choices modulo `M`.
constraints: 1 ≤ M ≤ 10^9 (`M` is arbitrary, not necessarily prime)

examples.explanation: Two components on 3 vertices means one isolated vertex and one joined pair. Pick which of the 3 edges to keep; the other two are deleted.

Either one isolated vertex plus a connected triple: 4 choices of the vertex times 4 connected graphs on 3 labelled vertices (3 paths and the triangle) = 16, or two pairs: 3 ways to pair up the vertices, each pair keeps its edge = 3. Total 19.
There are 38 connected labelled graphs on 4 vertices, and 38 mod 10 = 8.

hints: The kept edges form a spanning subgraph of the complete graph. You are counting labelled graphs on N vertices with exactly K connected components.

First count connected labelled graphs c[n]: all 2^(n(n-1)/2) graphs minus those that are disconnected. Classify a disconnected graph by the size s of the component containing vertex 1: C(n-1, s-1) * c[s] * 2^((n-s)(n-s-1)/2).

Then let g[n][k] be graphs on n vertices with k components, again splitting off the component containing vertex 1: g[n][k] = sum over s of C(n-1, s-1) * c[s] * g[n-s][k-1]. Since M need not be prime, build binomials with Pascal's triangle instead of using inverses.
